issues.body: The IPvFuture `literal_ok` branch still validates its tail with `is_iunreserved`, whose definition includes RFC 3987 `ucschar`. IPvFuture is inherited from RFC 3986 and restricts its tail to ASCII `unreserved / sub-delims / ":"`; RFC 3987 does not widen that production. Consequently `http://[v1.π]/datatype` is still accepted by `is_well_formed_absolute_iri` and can pass authored datatype validation despite being malformed. This is materially identical to the round-4 major finding.
issues.fix_hint: Add an ASCII RFC 3986 `unreserved` predicate and use it only for the IPvFuture tail. Add `http://[v1.π]/datatype` to `MALFORMED`, retain an adjacent valid case such as `http://[v7.host]/datatype`, and add a public expansion regression expecting `InvalidTypedValue` for the malformed datatype.
issues.title: IPvFuture validation still accepts non-ASCII host characters

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant. The round-4 major finding remains unchanged: the IPvFuture tail is still checked with RFC 3987 `is_iunreserved`, which admits non-ASCII `ucschar`, although RFC 3986 IPvFuture permits only ASCII `unreserved / sub-delims / ":"`. The malformed non-ASCII IPvFuture and public expansion-path regression are still absent, so `http://[v1.π]/datatype` remains accepted as a datatype IRI.
